intuition: Start with the empty subset. Add one number, save the new subset, and try adding later numbers. Then undo the choice and try the next alternative. Moving only to later positions gives every subset one path through the search, regardless of the order in which we discover it.

Choose indices in strictly increasing order. At any call, the current path is already one valid subset, including the empty initial path. Extending it with each available later index generates larger subsets while giving each selected-index sequence exactly one route through the search.

Backtracking reuses the path list: append a choice, explore its descendants, then remove it before trying a sibling. Results must store copies because their contents must survive those later changes. This method spends its dominant work constructing the required outputs rather than filtering duplicate permutations.

steps: For nums=[1,2,3], the initial call records [] before making any choice.
Choose index 0, producing path [1], and record it. Choose index 1 next and record [1,2].
From [1,2], choose index 2 and record [1,2,3]. Then remove 3 and return to the previous decision.
Backtrack to [1], skip index 1 on the next branch, and choose index 2 to record [1,3].
After removing 1, the root chooses index 1. Record [2] and its extension [2,3].
The root finally chooses index 2 and records [3]. These eight paths are exactly all subsets; their displayed order is unrestricted.

codeNotes.note: Record at every call, not only a leaf. Partial paths are themselves valid subsets, and copying preserves them during backtracking.
The available range excludes every earlier selected index, preventing repeated elements and alternate orderings of the same subset.
After choosing i, only later indices may extend the path. This creates one unique increasing-index representation for every subset.

keyDecision: Save a copy of the current subset at every call, including the empty starting call.
